title: When sustainability meets risk perception: an extended goal-directed behavior model of consumers' sustainable clothing purchase intentions
journal: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management: An International Journal
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop an extended model of goal-directed behavior (MGB) to explain consumers' sustainable clothing purchase behavior and the attitude–behavior gap by incorporating perceived risk into the original MGB framework. Design/methodology/approach Based on the MGB, an extended research model was developed by incorporating perceived aesthetic risk and perceived performance risk as moderating variables. Data were collected from 597 Chinese consumers through a questionnaire survey and analyzed using structural equation modeling with SmartPLS 4.0. Findings Attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, anticipated emotions and frequency of past behavior significantly influence consumers' desire, which in turn predicts purchase intention. Perceived aesthetic risk positively moderates the relationship between desire and purchase intention, whereas perceived performance risk has no significant moderating effect. Originality/value This study extends the MGB by distinguishing between perceived aesthetic risk and perceived performance risk as separate moderating variables and demonstrates the joint roles of cognitive, emotional and habitual processes in explaining sustainable clothing purchase behavior.

title: Value Generation, Risk Transmission and Collaborative Governance of "Sports Takeout"
journal: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
abstract: With the accelerated integration of digital platforms into the sports service sector, "sports takeout" has gradually become an emerging business format that meets personalized, instant and scenario-based fitness needs. To reveal its value generation logic and governance problems arising from its operation, this paper adopts the literature review method and logical analysis method to carry out research from three dimensions: platform organization, service fulfillment and risk transmission. The study concludes that through online matching, on-site fulfillment and continuous evaluation feedback, "sports takeout" reduces consumers' time and space costs, improves the accessibility of sports services and the efficiency of supply-demand matching, and can promote the shift of sports services from venue-centered to user-living-area-oriented. However, while platformization and mobilization create more convenient value, they also bring problems such as difficult identification of coach qualifications, difficulty in standardizing service quality, higher safety risk coefficients in non-fixed venues, insufficient personal information protection, and blurred boundaries of platform responsibilities. To promote "sports takeout" from a short-term consumption hotspot to a stable service format, we should take the service chain as the governance object, continuously improve mechanisms such as coach access, pre-class assessment, process traceability, data protection, liability insurance and dispute handling, and better build a collaborative governance system combining government supervision, platform accountability, industry self-discipline and consumer participation.

title: Urban-Rural Disparities in Long-Term Care Resources and Elderly Dignity in China: Policy Lessons from Japan's Community-Based Care System
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
abstract: China's rapid population aging has created growing demand for long-term care (LTC), but eldercare resources remain unevenly distributed between urban and rural areas. This paper will examine how inequality in LTC resources affects elderly people's ability to age with dignity and independence whilst drawing policy lessons from Japan's Community-Based Integrated Care System (CBICS). Rural older adults face faster aging, weak formal care infrastructure, fewer trained workers, lower purchasing power, and greater dependence on family caregivers. These conditions limit access to affordable, nearby, and adequate care whilst also restricting their social dignity by weakening their autonomy, privacy, and community belonging. This study explores Japan's CBICS, which offers elements including aging in place, local coordination, preventive care, medical-social integration, and community participation. This paper makes sure to acknowledge the model's imperfections to argue that China should adapt Japan's broader principles rather than copy its institutions directly. Ultimately, this paper argues that protecting elderly dignity in rural China requires a more equitable, community-based long-term care network that combines public financing, rural infrastructure, family caregiver support, and human-centered technology.

title: Unpacking retailer performance in the wine and spirits sector: multilevel support, satisfaction and the moderating power of digital enablement
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how perceived brand support and perceived salesperson support (PSS) influence retailer commercial performance (RCP) in the wine and spirits sector. Grounded in relationship marketing theory and a technology–organization–environment (TOE)-based perspective, it tests retailer satisfaction (RS) as a mediator and digital enablement (DE) as a moderator that strengthens the retailer satisfaction–retailer commercial performance (RS–RCP) relationship in a regulated, competitive distribution context. Design/methodology/approach Using a cross-sectional survey design, questionnaire data were obtained from 428 wine and spirits retailers and shop/showroom owners distributing products for international spirits groups in Vietnam. The hypothesized mediation–moderation model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings PBS and PSS positively affect RS, which in turn enhances RCP. RS mediates the relationships between perceived support and RCP, indicating that support translates into commercial outcomes through improved RS. Additionally, DE positively moderates the RS–RCP link, such that higher DE strengthens the effect of satisfaction on retailer outcomes. Practical implications Suppliers in the wine and spirits channel should integrate brand-level resources with problem-solving salesperson support to enhance RS. Investing in DE can further improve channel effectiveness by accelerating the translation of satisfaction into commercial performance in competitive point-of-sale environments. Originality/value This study extends channel and relationship marketing research by explaining how dual-source support translates into RCP through RS, while identifying DE as a key boundary condition. Empirically, it provides evidence from Vietnam's traditional trade context, where B2B channel dynamics remain underexplored compared to consumer-focused alcohol marketing.

title: Unlocking international SME success: the crucial role of dynamic managerial capabilities in driving international entrepreneurial orientation
abstract: Purpose The study aims to examine the relationship between international entrepreneurial orientation (IEO) and international performance (IP) of internationalized small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the Slovak Republic. Given the scarcity of empirical research on the managerial dimensions influencing this relationship, the study also aims to investigate the moderating effect of dynamic managerial capabilities (DMCs) as a higher-order variable and its components in the IEO-IP nexus. The theoretical framework is grounded in the resource-based view and capability-based view, which posit that firm-specific resources and capabilities are critical sources of competitive advantage. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via a questionnaire survey administered to 145 internationalized SMEs in the service and industrial sectors. The analysis used a robust statistical method, structural equation modelling through partial least squares, which is suitable for modeling complex relationships and managing smaller sample sizes. Findings The results reveal that IEO is directly associated with the IP of SMEs. Moreover, DMCs, as a multidimensional construct, exert a statistically significant moderating effect on the IEO-IP relationship. Regarding the specific components of DMCs, social capital and managerial cognition significantly reinforce the connection between IEO and international performance, while human capital does not exhibit a significant effect. Originality/value The study’s theoretical contribution lies in validating the role of DMCs as a complex construct in augmenting international performance in conjunction with IEO. It also identifies the differential effects of the three DMCs components in the IEO-IP framework, offering nuanced insights into their moderating roles. The research underscores the importance of strategic business orientation and DMCs for SMEs operating in the global market. Finally, managerial implications and directions for future research are proposed.

title: The paradox complex: how paradoxical thinking recursively generates new tensions and emotional strain in sustainability work
abstract: Purpose This study challenges the dominant assumption that paradoxical thinking is inherently superior for managing organizational tensions. Focusing on the sustainability-profitability tension, it explores how paradoxical and business case cognitive frames influence individual emotional and behavioral responses, revealing that paradoxical thinking can lead to unintended psychological and relational costs. Design/methodology/approach Using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis, this qualitative study draws on in-depth interviews with managers at a construction firm. It investigates how individuals cognitively frame the sustainability-profitability tension and how these frames shape their emotional experiences, actions and organizational relationships. Findings The study identifies three core dimensions Framing, Responding and Relating – that explain how individuals engage with tensions. Managers using a paradoxical frame perceived sustainability and profitability as interdependent and pursued both, yet experienced emotional strain, organizational disconnection and limited influence, resulting in what is termed a “paradox loop.” In contrast, managers using a business case frame subordinated sustainability to profitability and avoided personal engagement, which reduced emotional strain and maintained organizational alignment. The findings show that paradoxical thinking, while fostering nuanced sensemaking, does not necessarily yield more effective action or individual wellbeing. Originality/value This study contributes to paradox theory by integrating emotional dynamics into the microfoundations of paradox and introducing the concept of the paradox loop. It reveals that paradoxical cognition, while often idealized, can impose psychological burdens and hinder engagement. The study calls for more balanced, emotionally grounded understandings of paradoxical thinking in organizational contexts, particularly within corporate sustainability.

title: The grandparents’ role in shaping grandchildren’s physical activity
abstract: Abstract Little is known about how grandparents contribute to children’s physical activity, despite their increasing involvement in childcare. Guided by Bronfenbrenner’s ecological systems theory, this qualitative study aimed to explore the roles grandparents play in shaping their grandchildren’s physical activity. Seventeen family triads ( N = 64) participated in the study. In-depth semi-structured group interviews were conducted in a family setting or family-friendly location. Data were analyzed using open coding, and thematic analysis was supported by qualitative data analysis software. The results are summarized into themes clarifying grandparental roles. The analysis identified three main themes: grandparents as facilitators of physical activity opportunities; barriers to physical activity; and shared active lifestyles. Eight minor themes stemmed from these three main themes, in which participants expressed that grandparents are supportive of children’s physical activity and that children’s physical activity is viewed as a meaningful leisure activity. At the same time, barriers to grandparents’ provision of physical activity support for the child’s generation were identified, including grandparents’ health status and children’s increased preference for digital technology. However, support for physical activity through educational goals and chores, as well as evidence of intergenerational value transfer, was found. This study extends current knowledge about family influences on children’s physical activity beyond the parental generation and demonstrates how grandparental involvement can be understood within an ecological and intergenerational framework. The findings highlight the potential value of intentionally involving grandparents in policies, school and community programs, and family-based interventions to promote children’s physical activity.

title: Strategies for managing learner misbehaviour in Namibian schools: Learners’ perspective
journal: African Journal of Teacher Education and Development
abstract: Background: Managing learner misbehaviour is central to successful teaching and learning. As key players in the teaching and learning process, learners’ voices are important to consider when designing disciplinary frameworks. Aim: This article aimed to explore effective strategies for managing learner misbehaviour from learners’ perspectives, bridging the gap in which disciplinary policies are often implemented without consulting learners. Setting: Data were collected from 1262 learners across 78 secondary schools in all 14 education regions in Namibia. Methods: The study employed a mixed-methods approach using a convergent parallel design. Data were collected using a questionnaire containing closed and open-ended items. Responses from the closed-ended items were analysed using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) (IBM Corp, Armonk, NY, United States [US]), whereas the open-ended responses were analysed through thematic content analysis. Results: The study findings reveal that learners prefer relational and restorative interventions compared to punitive ones. Specifically, 81% of participants indicated that parental involvement is the most effective strategy, followed by private, one-on-one conversations. Conversely, the results reveal that traditional punitive measures such as corporal punishment and public shaming were rated as ineffective and damaging to the teacher-learner relationship. However, a contradictory finding emerged regarding serious offences: 67% of learners indicated it is necessary to involve law enforcement for major transgressions such as theft, fighting, or alcohol and drugs. Conclusion: The study concludes that schools should move from reactive, exclusionary practices towards a three-way model of behaviour management that is restorative, preventive and structured. Contribution: By focusing on learner-centred strategies, schools can foster more equitable and supportive environments conducive to academic success.
